corpus.files_by_ext.definition: tracked files by lowercase extension; `(none)` when no extension

corpus.docs_total.definition: tracked `.md` outside `web/` — the corpus every other family measures

corpus.docs_by_dir.definition: corpus documents by top-level directory; root files under `(root)`

corpus.docs_by_type.definition: corpus documents by frontmatter `type`; `(none)` when absent

corpus.docs_without_frontmatter.definition: corpus documents with no `---` block at the top

corpus.apparatus.definition: corpus documents classified apparatus by rules.json (`type: meta`, listed basename, or template path)

corpus.scripts_total.definition: files under `machine/scripts/` with a code extension (.py .mjs .js .sh .ts)

corpus.scripts_by_language.definition: those scripts by language, from the extension

corpus.scripts_in_ci.definition: guards the runner runs in CI: registered scripts under `machine/scripts/` (ENG-032)

series.registration.definition: per series with a naming scheme (rules.json): documents whose filename matches `<PREFIX>-<NNN>-` (or the daily `RPT-<date>` form in reports/) over documents in the series — excluding `_template/`, `reports/evidence/`, apparatus and frozen artefacts (by filename shape). Same predicate as `count-evidence.py matricula`.

series.agents_folder_named.definition: directories under `agents/` other than `_template` — identified by folder name, no prefix by design (ADR-005 v1.1.0)

missions.by_guild.definition: by frontmatter `guild`; `(none)` when absent or null-like

missions.by_territory.definition: by frontmatter `territory`; `TBA` folds into `(none)`, reported separately as `territory_tba`

missions.territory_tba.definition: `territory: TBA` (ADR-028 deferral; owner MIS-124 closed 2026-09-09, zero territory TBA remains)

missions.done_without_closure.definition: `status: done` with no `## Closure` heading (MIS-134 strict form)

missions.done_without_closure_tolerant.definition: `status: done` with none of the five closure headings MIS-134 tolerates

missions.started_with_offset.definition: `started` written with a UTC offset instead of `Z`

tokens.tokenizer.definition: rank file cl100k_base.tiktoken, sha256 223921b76ee99bde995b7ff738513eef100fb51d18c93597a113bcffe865b2a7 (the hash tiktoken itself pins); encoder machine/scripts/lib/cl100k.mjs, equal to tiktoken.encode_ordinary over every document by test

tokens.total.definition: Σ tokens over the corpus (every tracked .md outside web/, whole file, frontmatter included)

tokens.by_dir.definition: tokens per top-level dir, largest first

tokens.by_status.definition: tokens per frontmatter status ((none) = no status), largest first

tokens.largest.definition: the five largest documents as [path, tokens]

headers.docs_with_frontmatter.definition: docs whose text opens with a --- block the shared reader parses

headers.field_usage.definition: per frontmatter key, the number of docs carrying it, most used first

headers.uid_collisions.definition: Σ(n−1) over uid values held by n>1 docs; values as typed (a shared placeholder counts)

headers.uid_collision_values.definition: the colliding uid values with their holder counts

headers.created_T000000Z.definition: created ending in the midnight-UTC placeholder

headers.hygiene.definition: frontmatter-census.py §4: created/updated without time; empty values; version with v prefix; values matching TODO|TBD|FIXME|{{|<…>|xxx

provenance.authorship.definition: nature of author: per doc, `author:` normalised → human (Oracle aliases) · ai-persona (agents whose SOUL.md declares a model, list of 2026-08-26) · ai-model (name matches claude|gpt|opus|sonnet|fable|gemini|llm) · other · no-author · no-frontmatter

provenance.dates_vs_commits_compared.definition: docs with a created date AND a first-add commit found by one `git log --diff-filter=AR -M` walk (renames followed)

provenance.created_ahead_of_commit.definition: created day later than the day the file was first added to git (dates-vs-commits.py "DISCREPA", over the whole corpus, not the post-tag set)

provenance.created_behind_commit.definition: created day earlier than the first-add commit — expected for migrated or backdated documents; counted, not judged

provenance.regime_crossings.definition: renames in history (git -M) whose source and target resolve to different REUSE.toml licences (last matching annotation wins); regime-crossings.py

provenance.protocol_anchor.definition: P-003 rule as protocol-anchor.py applies it: status ∈ {done,frozen,cancelled,backlog} is Oracle-set → anchored if owner=oracle, anchored-weak if another owner, anchored-no-owner if none; other states not-oracle-state. The CYCLE_* timestamp evidence it also used lived in /tmp and is not reproducible

contradictions.status_vocabulary_used.definition: frontmatter status values in the corpus with counts

contradictions.status_vocabulary_undecla.definition: status values in use that machine/scripts/lib/rules.json does not declare (STD-016 lifecycles), with the docs carrying them — a contradiction between a document and the vocabulary

contradictions.ci_marked_scripts_not_in_.definition: scripts a Check row of a standard names that the runner does not run in CI — a norm claiming a machine check that does not happen

contradictions.ci_scripts_not_marked.definition: scripts the runner runs in CI that no Check row of any standard names — a check the norm does not claim

contradictions.id_form_per_series.definition: per series prefix, citations by digit width (3 vs 4) across the corpus; S1 fixes 4 for MIS files, 3 in `id:`

contradictions.id_form_mixed.definition: prefixes cited with more than one digit width — the class is contradictory for these

contradictions.claims_open.definition: claims.json entries whose exact quote is still at its path

contradictions.claims_resolved.definition: entries whose quote is no longer in any tracked .md

contradictions.claims_moved.definition: entries whose quote left its path and is found in another tracked .md — meaningful only for quotes unique to one file; a short quote (`status: draft`) can only be open or resolved at its own path

value.claim: The protocol that governs how every series is named, renamed and closed — cited by ADR-005, STD-001 and the missions — is itself draft. Deferred: the Oracle signs.

STD-004's Ring 3 registry still lists fields the corpus no longer carries as registered. Deferred → STD-004 v1.5.0. Anchor re-pointed 2026-09-03: the original quote lived in an amendment note removed when STD-004 was slimmed to v2.0.0; the registry row it denounces is unchanged, so the claim stays open. Anchor re-pointed 2026-09-09: the registry row moved whole into the register STD-016 under ADR-043.
web/** → MIT while MIS-065's criterion that no culture-branch content is matched by it is unverified. Deferred → DBT-005.
Parameterised redirect that check-url-lifecycle matches literally — neither verified nor expanded. Deferred: design choice.
done missions without a filled ## Closure — the guard is a proposal, not a guard; the count is missions.done_without_closure in this dataset. Deferred → MIS-134.

contradictions.claims.definition: the register, verified this run: id, severity (MIS-135: A norm↔norm/guard · B norm↔corpus · C housekeeping), state, where (path#line when open), claim

figures.live.definition: lines in non-apparatus docs outside machine/telemetry/ (frontmatter and code fences excluded) that state a corpus-shaped figure — "N tokens|documents|files|missions", "N/M", "N %" — with no `@ <7-hex head>` on the line. A detector, not a verdict: dated tables and closed records legitimately carry such lines

figures.live_by_doc.definition: the fifteen docs with most such lines

figures.cited.definition: citations in the §10.5 form `key = value @ head` across the corpus

figures.stale_citations.definition: cited `key = value @ head` whose value in latest.json at this HEAD differs from the cited value: [where, key, cited, current]. A stale citation is not an error — the head beside it says when it was true
